select: “NYC Restaurant Inspections”

Step 0. Import

Step 1. Data cleaning, defining my time range: 2016.1.1 - 2019.2.1

inspection_period =
  rest_inspec |>
  mutate(inspection_date = as.Date(inspection_date)) |>
  filter(
    inspection_date >= as.Date("2016-01-01"),
    inspection_date < as.Date("2019-02-01")
  )
inspection_summary =
  inspection_period |>
  group_by(camis, inspection_date, inspection_type) |>
  summarize(
    n_violations = n_distinct(violation_code, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_scores = n_distinct(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    inspection_score = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE),
  ) |>
  ungroup()
## `summarise()` has regrouped the output.
## ℹ Summaries were computed grouped by camis, inspection_date, and
##   inspection_type.
## ℹ Output is grouped by camis and inspection_date.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.groups = "drop_last")` to silence this message.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.by = c(camis, inspection_date, inspection_type))` for
##   per-operation grouping (`?dplyr::dplyr_by`) instead.

Summarize each restaurant’s cumulative violation score during period 2016.1.1-2019.2.1.

restaurant_scores =
  inspection_summary |>
  filter(n_scores == 1) |>
  group_by(camis) |>
  summarize(total_score = sum(inspection_score))
#I only select those who only have one type of violation (because violation score is already a total)

I’m planning to do three graphs reflect relevant violation score x restaurant’s association during period 2016.1.1-2019.2.1: 1. A scatter plot reflects restaurant’s geographic location and its cumulative violation score, 2. A boxplot showcases restaurant’s cuisine type against the violation counts 3. A bar chart showcasesrestaurant’s cuisine type against the total violation scores, if that restaurant only has one kind of score that day.
